scale_001:n1.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the review criteria and competencies framework for our quarterly performance review cycle. This requires my final sign-off before anything is finalized or shared with the team.

First, ask me for: (1) our company name/domain and stage (startup size, industry), (2) the list of roles or departments we need criteria for (e.g., engineering, sales, design, ops), (3) any existing values, mission statement, or culture docs I want reflected, and (4) whether we want separate competencies for individual contributors vs. managers.

Once I provide this, draft a complete review criteria document that includes:
- A set of core company-wide competencies (e.g., communication, ownership, collaboration, execution) with a short definition for each
- Role-specific or department-specific competencies tailored to the roles I listed, drawing on common industry frameworks for similar roles and stage of company
- A simple rating scale (e.g., 1-5 or below/meets/exceeds expectations) with a one-line description of what each rating level means
- Notes on how self-assessments, manager reviews, and calibration should each map to these criteria (e.g., same criteria used across all three, or manager-only competencies)

Organize the draft clearly by section (Company-Wide Competencies, Role-Specific Competencies, Rating Scale, Usage Notes) so it's easy for leadership to review and edit.

Do not finalize, publish, or share this framework with employees or managers. This is a draft for leadership judgment about what the company values and how to measure it — present the completed draft to me, flag any assumptions you made, and then stop for human sign-off so I and other leaders can review, adjust, and approve before it's used in the review cycle.

scale_001:n2.prompt:
You are helping me configure quarterly performance review templates in BambooHR. Before starting, ask me for any of the following you don't already have: my BambooHR company domain/subdomain, confirmation that you should use my configured BambooHR credentials to access the account, and the review cycle details I want reflected in the templates — specifically: (1) the self-assessment questions or sections (e.g., accomplishments, goals progress, growth areas), (2) the manager review questions or sections (e.g., performance against goals, competencies, overall rating), (3) the rating scale to use (e.g., 1-5, or descriptive labels), (4) any competency or values framework to include, and (5) whether calibration notes/fields should be built into the manager template or handled separately.

Once you have these inputs, log into BambooHR using my configured credentials and, in the Performance Management settings, draft the review templates: create a self-assessment template with the specified questions/sections, create a manager review template with the specified questions, rating scale, and competency fields, and note where calibration-related fields fit into the manager template if applicable. Do not publish, activate, assign to employees, or launch the review cycle — only prepare the templates in draft/inactive form within BambooHR (or as a written draft if the interface requires activation to save).

When done, report back: a summary of each template's structure (sections, questions, rating scale, competencies), where the drafts currently sit in BambooHR (e.g., saved as draft, template name/ID), and any settings or fields you were unable to fully configure. Then stop for human sign-off — do not activate templates, assign them to review cycles, or notify employees until I explicitly approve.

scale_001:n3.prompt:
You are helping me launch the self-assessment stage of our quarterly performance review cycle in BambooHR. If you don't already have them, ask me for: our BambooHR company subdomain/URL, the name of the performance review cycle already configured (or the review template to use), the list of employees or department(s) who should receive self-assessment forms, the response deadline date, and any custom message/instructions to include in the notification email.

Using your configured credentials, log into our BambooHR account and navigate to the Performance module. Locate or confirm the review cycle for this quarter, verify the self-assessment template is attached, and build the full send-out: select the correct employee list, set the due date I gave you, and draft the notification/reminder email text using any custom instructions I provided. Do not click send or launch the review cycle yet — prepare everything (the recipient list, template selection, due date, and draft email copy) as a clear summary I can review, including a checklist of exactly what will happen when it's sent (who receives it, what date it's due, what template they'll fill out).

Because this step requires my explicit approval before changes are applied, once your preparation is complete, stop for human sign-off. Do not send the forms or activate the cycle yourself.

Report back with: the review cycle name, the employee count and list (or a link to it in BambooHR), the due date, the draft notification email text, and confirmation that everything is staged and awaiting my approval to send.

scale_001:n4.prompt:
You are helping me track completion of employee self-assessments for our quarterly performance review cycle. This step is a third-party-wait: employees must personally write and submit their own self-assessments in their own time, which remains a human step you cannot perform or accelerate.

Before starting, ask me for anything you need that isn't already available, such as: the list of employees due for review, the tool we use to distribute/collect self-assessments (e.g. Google Docs, Notion, BambooHR, Lattice, a shared spreadsheet, or email), the due date for this cycle, and where I want status tracked (e.g. a spreadsheet or doc you have access to).

Your job:
1. Using the employee list, set up or update a simple tracking log (in the spreadsheet/doc I specify or one you create) with columns: Employee Name, Self-Assessment Status (Not Started / In Progress / Submitted), Date Submitted, Notes.
2. If I ask you to send reminders, draft a polite reminder message referencing the due date, and prepare it for me to review — do not send anything on my behalf without my confirmation.
3. On a schedule I specify (e.g. daily or every few days), check the collection tool/location for newly submitted self-assessments using your configured credentials, and update the tracking log accordingly.
4. Flag any employees who are approaching or past the due date without a submission.

Done looks like: a working tracking log reflecting current submission status for all employees, with drafted (unsent) reminder messages ready for my review if requested.

Report back to me with: the current count of Submitted vs Not Started/In Progress, a list of overdue employees, and confirmation that submission collection remains a human step dependent on each employee completing their own reflection.

scale_001:n5.prompt:
You are helping me manage the 'Managers write reviews' step of our quarterly performance review cycle. This is a human-judgment step: each manager must personally evaluate and finalize the review for their direct report. Your job is to prepare everything so managers can move quickly, but you must not write, finalize, or submit any manager's evaluation or judgment on their behalf.

First, ask me for anything missing: (1) the name of the performance review platform we use (e.g., our HRIS or dedicated review tool), (2) the list of managers and their direct reports for this cycle, (3) where to find each employee's goals, metrics, and any peer feedback already collected, and (4) the review deadline.

Then, for each manager: gather the relevant employee's goals, performance metrics, and peer feedback, and assemble a pre-filled draft review outline (structured by whatever categories our template uses) that summarizes the source data factually, without inserting ratings, opinions, or judgment calls. Save or attach this draft in the review tool against the correct employee record, or produce it as a document for the manager if the tool doesn't support drafts.

Since this step is async, track and report which managers have draft materials ready, which have not yet started or finalized their actual review, and flag any missing input data (e.g., no goals on file, no peer feedback). Poll or check back on completion status if the tool allows, and report the up-to-date list of pending vs. completed reviews.

Do not finalize, rate, edit judgment content, or submit any review — that decision and action belongs solely to each manager. Prepare the drafts and checklist, then stop for human sign-off.

scale_001:n6.prompt:
You are helping me prepare for a quarterly performance review calibration meeting where managers and HR will negotiate and reconcile ratings across teams against a limited promotion/comp budget. The actual live negotiation is a human discussion and remains a human step — you cannot run or simulate it. Your job is to prepare all the supporting materials beforehand.

Please ask me for anything you need that isn't already available, such as: the location of self-assessment and manager review data (e.g., a shared spreadsheet, Google Sheets export, or HR system export), the rating scale used, the list of participating managers/teams, and the approximate promotion/comp budget constraints for this cycle.

Once you have the data, do the following:
1. Compile a consolidated roster showing each employee's self-assessment rating and manager rating side by side, flagging any large discrepancies.
2. Produce a summary of rating distribution per manager/team (e.g., counts per rating level) so outliers or leniency/severity patterns are visible.
3. Draft an agenda for the calibration meeting covering: review of distributions, discussion order (e.g., by discrepancy size or by team), and time allocation.
4. Prepare a blank decision-tracking sheet (employee, original rating, discussed rating, final rating, rationale, approver) for use live during the meeting.
5. List any known budget constraints alongside the roster so the group can see capacity limits while discussing.

Done looks like: a consolidated data sheet, discrepancy flags, distribution summary, draft agenda, and blank decision-tracking template all ready to send to participants ahead of the meeting.

Report back with links or file locations for each artifact, a brief summary of notable discrepancies or patterns you found, and then stop for human sign-off before the meeting, since the actual calibration negotiation and final rating decisions must be made by the managers and HR in person.

scale_001:n7.prompt:
You are helping me deliver quarterly performance reviews and schedule follow-up 1:1s using our team-chat tool, {{vendor}}. If you don't already have them, ask me for: (1) the list of employees due reviews this cycle with their {{vendor}} channel or DM identifiers, (2) the finalized review content/summary for each employee (or tell me if it needs drafting from calibration notes I provide), and (3) my preferred 1:1 scheduling windows for the next two weeks.

For each employee, prepare: a draft delivery message summarizing their review (strengths, growth areas, rating context) suitable for sending as a direct message or channel post via the {{vendor}} messaging API, and a proposed 1:1 meeting time slot with a note that the meeting will use {{vendor}}'s built-in call feature (audio/video call started directly from the DM, with screen share available for walking through the review together). Do not send anything yet.

Compile all drafts and proposed 1:1 times into a single checklist, organized by employee name, showing: the message text ready to send, the proposed meeting time, and how the call will be initiated in {{vendor}}. Flag any employees missing review content or scheduling availability.

Because a human must explicitly approve before any changes are applied, present this complete checklist to me for review and then stop for human sign-off — do not send any messages, post anything, or create any calendar/meeting invites until I explicitly approve each item. Report back with the full checklist and a summary count of how many reviews are ready to send versus how many need more input from me.
